stimulus.title: Light intensity and net oxygen production
stimulus.description: An aquatic plant was exposed to increasing light intensity while carbon dioxide concentration and temperature were kept constant.
stimulus.note: Negative net oxygen production indicates that respiration exceeds photosynthetic oxygen release.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Estimate the light intensity at which net oxygen production is zero.
markscheme: Approximately 0.8 relative units (accept a reasonable estimate between 0 and 1).
markschemeJa: 約0.8相対単位（0〜1の妥当な推定を認める）。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Describe the relationship between light intensity and net oxygen production.
markscheme: Net oxygen production increases strongly as light intensity rises from low values.
At higher light intensities the increase becomes small and the rate approaches a plateau near 6.3 relative units min⁻¹.
markschemeJa: 低い範囲では光強度が上がると正味酸素生成量が大きく増える。
高い光強度では増加幅が小さくなり、約6.3 relative units min⁻¹付近で頭打ちになる。
parts.modelAnswer: Net oxygen production rises with light intensity at first, then levels off at high light intensity.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 正味酸素生成量は最初は光強度とともに増加しますが、高い光強度では頭打ちになります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why the graph approaches a plateau at high light intensity.
markscheme: Light is no longer the main limiting factor once sufficient light is available.
Another factor such as carbon dioxide availability, temperature or photosynthetic enzyme capacity limits the maximum rate.
markschemeJa: 十分な光があると光は主要な制限要因ではなくなる。
二酸化炭素供給、温度、光合成酵素の処理能力など別の要因が最大速度を制限する。
parts.modelAnswer: At high light intensity, light is no longer limiting; another factor such as carbon dioxide concentration or enzyme capacity limits photosynthesis.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 高い光強度では光が制限要因ではなくなり、二酸化炭素濃度や酵素能力など別の要因が光合成速度を制限します。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: State one reason why net oxygen production is negative in darkness.
markscheme: Photosynthesis stops without light while cellular respiration continues and consumes oxygen.
markschemeJa: 暗所では光合成が停止する一方、細胞呼吸は続いて酸素を消費する。
parts.modelAnswer: In darkness photosynthesis stops but respiration continues, so oxygen is consumed overall.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 暗所では光合成が止まっても呼吸は続くため、全体として酸素が消費されます。

stimulus.title: Relative abundance of cell components
stimulus.description: The table compares selected features in three specialized human cell types. Values are relative units.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the cell type most specialized for secretion of large amounts of protein.
markscheme: Pancreatic secretory cell, because it has the highest relative abundance of rough endoplasmic reticulum.
markschemeJa: 粗面小胞体が最も多いため、膵臓の分泌細胞。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why cardiac muscle cells contain many mitochondria.
markscheme: Cardiac muscle contracts continuously and has a high ATP demand.
Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and supply ATP for repeated contraction and ion transport.
markschemeJa: 心筋は継続的に収縮するためATP需要が高い。
ミトコンドリアで好気呼吸が行われ、反復収縮やイオン輸送に必要なATPを供給する。
parts.modelAnswer: Cardiac muscle has a high, continuous ATP demand. Many mitochondria support aerobic respiration and ATP supply for contraction.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 心筋は継続的に多くのATPを必要とするため、ミトコンドリアが多く、好気呼吸で収縮に必要なATPを供給します。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how abundant microvilli support the function of small-intestine epithelial cells.
markscheme: Microvilli greatly increase the membrane surface area available for absorption.
The larger surface can contain more transport proteins and allows faster uptake of digested nutrients.
markschemeJa: 微絨毛は吸収に利用できる膜表面積を大きく増やす。
広い表面にはより多くの輸送タンパク質を配置でき、消化産物の吸収を速める。
parts.modelAnswer: Microvilli increase surface area, allowing more transport proteins and faster nutrient absorption.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 微絨毛は表面積を増やし、より多くの輸送タンパク質を配置して栄養吸収を速めます。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: State the biological process that explains how cells with the same genome can develop these different structures.
markscheme: Differential gene expression / cell differentiation.
markschemeJa: 遺伝子発現の違い／細胞分化。
parts.modelAnswer: Differential gene expression during cell differentiation.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 細胞分化に伴う遺伝子発現の違いです。

stimulus.title: Water potential and change in leaf-disc mass
stimulus.description: Equal leaf discs were placed for 30 minutes in solutions with known water potentials.
stimulus.note: Positive values indicate an increase in disc mass.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Estimate the water potential of the leaf tissue.
markscheme: Approximately −0.68 MPa (accept a reasonable estimate between −0.60 and −0.80 MPa).
markschemeJa: 約−0.68 MPa（−0.60〜−0.80 MPaの妥当な推定を認める）。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Calculate the difference in mean mass change between −0.20 MPa and −1.00 MPa solutions.
markscheme: The numerical difference is 6.8 − (−5.6) = 12.4 percentage points.
The result is correctly expressed as a 12.4 percentage-point difference.
markschemeJa: 差は6.8－（−5.6）＝12.4パーセントポイント。
12.4パーセントポイントの差として正しく表す。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why the leaf discs lose mass in the −1.00 MPa solution.
markscheme: The external solution has a lower (more negative) water potential than the leaf cells.
Water moves out of the cells by osmosis across partially permeable membranes, decreasing tissue mass.
markschemeJa: 外液は葉の細胞より低い（より負の）水ポテンシャルをもつ。
水が部分透過性膜を通って浸透により細胞外へ移動し、組織質量が減少する。
parts.modelAnswer: The −1.00 MPa solution has lower water potential, so water leaves the cells by osmosis and the discs lose mass.
parts.modelAnswerJa: −1.00 MPa溶液の方が水ポテンシャルが低いため、水が浸透によって細胞外へ出て質量が減少します。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Suggest two improvements that would make the estimate of tissue water potential more precise and reliable.
markscheme: Use more solution water potentials with smaller intervals around the zero mass-change point.
Use replicate discs at each water potential and calculate mean values, while controlling disc size, time and temperature.
markschemeJa: 質量変化0付近でより細かい間隔の水ポテンシャルを多数用いる。
各条件で複数の反復を行い平均を求め、ディスク大きさ、時間、温度などを一定にする。
parts.modelAnswer: Use smaller water-potential intervals near the zero point and replicate leaf discs at each value to calculate a mean.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 0点付近の水ポテンシャル間隔を細かくし、各条件で複数の葉ディスクを使って平均を求めます。

stimulus.title: Differences in a homologous DNA sequence among four species
stimulus.description: The same 600-base homologous DNA region was compared pairwise among four species.
stimulus.note: Lower numbers indicate fewer sequence differences in the region analysed.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the pair of species with the fewest nucleotide differences.
markscheme: Species P and Q, with 6 nucleotide differences.
markschemeJa: 塩基差が6で最も少ないPとQ。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage of nucleotide positions that differ between species P and Q in this 600-base region.
markscheme: Percentage difference = 6 ÷ 600 × 100.
The percentage difference is 1.0%.
markschemeJa: 差の割合は6÷600×100で計算する。
塩基差の割合は1.0%。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Infer the relative evolutionary relationships among the four species using the sequence data.
markscheme: P and Q are inferred to be the most closely related pair because they have the fewest sequence differences.
R and S are also relatively closely related to each other compared with their differences from P or Q, suggesting two closer groupings, P-Q and R-S.
markschemeJa: PとQは配列差が最も少ないため、最も近縁な組と推定される。
RとSもPまたはQとの比較より互いの差が少なく、P-QとR-Sという2つのより近いグループが示唆される。
parts.modelAnswer: P and Q are the closest pair. R and S also form a relatively close pair, while comparisons between the P-Q group and the R-S group show more differences.
parts.modelAnswerJa: PとQが最も近縁です。RとSも比較的近い組で、P-Q群とR-S群の間ではより多くの配列差が見られます。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Suggest one limitation of inferring evolutionary relationships from this dataset alone.
markscheme: Only one DNA region was analysed; using additional independent genes or whole-genome data would provide stronger evidence.
markschemeJa: 1つのDNA領域しか解析していないため、複数の独立した遺伝子や全ゲノムデータを用いるとより強い証拠になる。
parts.modelAnswer: Only one DNA region was compared, so additional independent sequence data would strengthen the inference.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 1つのDNA領域だけの比較なので、他の独立した配列データも用いると推定の信頼性が高まります。
